models.title: Trade-weighted Marshall–Lerner response expression
models.summary: The text weights the two demand elasticities by export and import shares and compares the expression with zero.

relationship.original_equation: Weighted response = export weight × export elasticity + import weight × (import elasticity − 1)
relationship.translation_notes: Inputs and output are dimensionless. The subtraction from 1 creates the import share and elasticity offset.

assumptions: Elasticities are nonnegative magnitudes of export and import demand responses and use the sign convention of the assigned source.
Export and import weights are fractions of the same total trade, so the import weight is one minus the export weight.
The stated local analysis assumes full exchange-rate pass-through and the source model’s other-things-equal conditions.
limitations: A positive score is a model condition, not a guarantee of an actual improvement in the trade balance.
Brookings uses weights normalized by domestic output; dividing both weights by their positive sum preserves the sign but changes the scale of its response coefficient.
Estimated elasticities, nonlinear adjustment, pass-through and income effects create substantial uncertainty.

relationship.translation_notes: All inputs and output are dimensionless base-one fractions; 1 is the direct price-effect coefficient.

assumptions: Elasticity is a positive magnitude; the NYU source instead uses signed negative demand elasticity.

limitations: This is a first-order approximation: finite changes include a price-quantity interaction and elasticity may vary.
Results describe a local mathematical response, not an actual prediction or trading recommendation.
